concept.name: Weekly review
concept.definition: A weekly aggregation and analysis of the trading journal - process metrics, outcome statistics by setup, recurring errors, and psychological patterns - used to adjust the playbook and plan on a sample less noisy than daily results. It produces a small number of concrete, testable adjustments rather than wholesale rewrites.
concept.intuition: Days are noise; the week is the first window where your actual habits become visible as data.
concept.mechanics: Compiles the week's trades: adherence rate, expectancy and R-distribution per setup, error counts by type, best and worst conditions; conclusions become at most a few documented changes (drop a setup, cap a time window, adjust a review step), which are then tracked for effect in subsequent weeks.
concept.failure_modes: A week is still a small sample - structural strategy changes on five days of data are overfitting to noise. Reviews without structured journal data become mood summaries rather than analysis.
concept.misconceptions: Weekly review is not a performance verdict; it is hypothesis generation for the plan. Nor is more analysis always better - the output should be a short list of testable adjustments.
concept.example: Friday's review shows all of the week's losses came from opening-range trades taken before 9:45; the plan is amended to exclude that window and the change is re-evaluated the following week.

citations.source: Brett N. Steenbarger, The Psychology of Trading: Tools and Techniques for Minding the Markets (Wiley, 2003) - publisher page
